text.p: European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros said on Monday he may drop out of this week's Tournament Players Championship because of a sore back and might even consider surgery.
Ballesteros, who withdrew from this weekend's British PGA Championship at Wentworth before the start of Friday's second round said he would make a decision on the Hamburg tournament later this week.
"I am still a little worried because my back is still bad," said Ballesteros.
"I will give it a couple of days and then decide about pulling out and maybe I will have to think about an operation."
The European Tour's head physiotherapist, Guy Delacour, has advised the Spaniard to rest for a couple of weeks following his latest setback.

Dropping out of the PGA had already cost the 40-year-old Spaniard the chance of a lucrative haul of Ryder Cup points in his bid to be the playing captain in the September match against the Americans at Valderrama.
He is currently 29th on the list, mainly as a result of his form late last year. This year he has missed the halfway cut in six of his eight tournaments.
But he has not abandoned hope. "I know that things can switch very quickly and I hope they will," he said.
"There is always a hope. But this has been going on a long time. I have waited a long time to take one step forward."

Ballesteros, who maintained that his game is improving despite his poor form and his opening 76 at Wentworth, stuck by his pronouncement that no one, not even Nick Faldo, was guaranteed of selection if thay had not automatically qualified.
"The situation is very clear. I don't think it is fair to the others to say he will definitely have a wild card.
"But Nick is playing very well and still has a good chance of making the team on the events he is still playing."
The qualification period for the September 26-28 match is August 31 with the top 10 getting team places before Ballesteros selects the remaining two.
Faldo had scheduled five more eligible events before then, besides the PGA where he was joint third entering Monday's final round.
